messages:
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: config-only canary for routing-service. Version: v2.3.1-configA. Rollout plan: 5% -> 25% over 15m, then 100% gated if metrics stable. Change window: 2026-03-20 17:00-18:00 UTC. Deploy ID: deploy-3056789123. Please ack.
anjali: ack. I'm on watch for latency, errors, and routing misroutes. No other routing config merges in the window pls. :eyes:
matt: quick note — this lowers request timeout to 8s and adjusts route weight caps. lgtm but check batching params (batch_max_tokens and batch_window_ms) in canary.
raul: adding small smoke test to run against canary endpoints (will post results). Also preflight: run `curl -H 'x-test: canary'` against /v1/route-check.
sara: canary started at 5% now. monitoring dashboards up. p95 baseline saved.
jon: FYI reduced per-route concurrency from 120 -> 80 for these traffic tiers.
anjali: posting the config snippet we're applying:
```
route_policy:
  prefer_local: true
  weight_overrides:
    blue: 0.05
    green: 0.95
limits:
  request_timeout_ms: 8000
  per_route_concurrency: 80
batching:
  batch_max_tokens: 1536
  batch_window_ms: 12
  kv_cache_prefixing: true
```
matt: that batch_window tweak (12ms) should help tail latency, but watch for tokenization edge cases. If we see rebuffering, rollback throttles.
raul: smoke tests: 200 reqs across canary: 0.5% 5xx, all from a single test client (flaky). p50 latency +3ms, p95 +9ms. pushing logs to #eng-monitoring.
sara: metrics: overall qps -1.8%, p95 +11ms (within SLO). error rate unchanged. cost-per-token slightly lower with batching. no spikes in retry counts.
anjali: proceeding to 25% in 10m if no regressions. oncall-bot will watch for alerts and auto-rollback threshold:
- alert if p95 delta > 50ms
- alert if 5xx rate increase > 0.5%
- alert if routing-misroute count > 10/min
oncall-bot: Auto-rollback enabled for deploy-3056789123 with thresholds above. If triggered, rollback command will be `deploy rollback deploy-3056789123 --reason auto`.
jon: manual rollback play if needed: `/deploy rollback deploy-3056789123` (needs ENG_RELEASES and oncall ack). I'll be ready to run if we see cascade.
matt: minor observation: pinning model variant for low-tier customers — make sure we pushed fallback variants; otherwise some requests could be routed to older kernels. Confirmed? 
anjali: confirmed we pinned fallback variant v2.2.9-fallback for the 3 low-latency customer groups.
raul: quick question — do we want to enable kv_cache_prefixing for all tenants now or just canary? current change flips it on globally in this config.
anjali: keep it global; previous tests show safe with small mem bump. monitor cache-miss ratio.
sara: 12m into 25% rollout now. telemetry stable. no increase in throttles. logs show small uptick in cache fills.
anjali: good. holding for the remainder of the window then finish to 100% if steady. tagging docs for release notes: note config-only, limits reduced, batching tightened, kv_cache prefixing on.
matt: also adding a short blurb for changelog about potential p95 improvement for high QPS clients and request-timeout change.
anjali: final check: if any team sees an anomaly, call rollback and ping #incidents. Otherwise finish ramp at +30m.
sara: no anomalies. Marking as green.
deploy-bot: Rollout progressed: 25% -> 100% completed at 2026-03-20T17:38:30Z for deploy-3056789123. Post-deploy hooks run.
oncall-bot: Post-deploy checks: all clear. No auto-rollback triggered. Summary: p95 delta +10ms, 5xx delta +0.02%.
anjali: thanks team. I'll close the window and add release note entry. :tada:
jon: recording rollback lesson: keep an easy one-line rollback command in the PR body for config-only deploys.
anjali: noted. closing thread.
